historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Tetracycline antibiotics

starting.description: In a planned search for microbial antibacterials, a yellow colony from a Missouri soil sample inhibited the team's initial bacterial panel; its antibiotic product was developed as aureomycin, later chlortetracycline. The detailed screen is a retrospective account, while the inventor's patent and the first page of his 1948 report describe a soil-derived producer and antibacterial substance.

inspiration.description: Observed bacterial growth inhibition by soil actinomycete cultures supplied active natural-product leads: aureomycin and, in a separate screen, terramycin.

steps.description: A planned soil screen identified an inhibitory organism in sample A-377, and its antibacterial product was developed as aureomycin.
Duggar described fermentation and separation to make the natural product available for study and use.
A separate soil screen identified the S. rimosus product terramycin, later called oxytetracycline, which shares the tetracycline family architecture.

Researchers modified active natural leads: aureomycin was dechlorinated to tetracycline, while oxytetracycline was modified via methacycline to doxycycline. A patent documents hydrogenation and separation of 6-deoxy-5-oxytetracycline isomers during this structural development.

design.description: Researchers selected and cultivated the producer, developed fermentation and recovery, then chemically modified existing active tetracyclines, including dechlorination of aureomycin and oxytetracycline modification through methacycline to doxycycline. The latter involved substantive structural and antibacterial-activity work, not only delivery optimization.

circumstances.description: The search and antimicrobial assays, as well as later chemical modifications, were deliberate. This describes those stages, not whether every individual hit was anticipated.

limits: Aureomycin and terramycin are separately discovered natural-product leads in the same established class. Doxycycline development is traced from the oxytetracycline branch; later semisynthetic engineering does not make the class origin design from scratch.
The record does not reconstruct the independent developmental or synthetic histories of all later tetracycline derivatives.
gaps: Only the first page of the 1948 Duggar journal report was read; its remaining pages were inaccessible. The 1950 Finlay report is located but unread. The detailed A-377 screening narrative comes from Nelson and Levy's retrospective, whose upstream 1969 book was not read.
The later drug name doxycycline is supplied by the retrospective, not asserted to appear in the passages read from the 1965 derivative patent.
